headline: Learned representations integrate multi-omics and single-cell data
label: Multimodal Omics Representation Learning
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply deep, transformer and autoencoder models to high-dimensional multi-omics and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representation of high-dimensional biomedical data, where model architecture rather than hand-specified features carries the inference step. Dynomap learns task-optimized spatial feature maps from unordered tabular data so that vision models can operate on it, while HSSE builds multiscale cell-level features from scRNA-seq via persistent sheaf Laplacians. MUST and Triad-LMF address multimodal integration: MUST handles missing pathology or genomics in TCGA survival prediction through diffusion-based generation, and Triad-LMF uses hierarchical low-rank fusion for cancer subtype classification. i-IF-Learn couples adaptive feature selection with unsupervised clustering, and the Boosting Autoencoder workflow reduces single-cell ligand-receptor interaction data. The shared novelty is explicit encoding of structure, whether multiscale, low-rank, or spatial, inside the representation rather than in preprocessing. Tissue geometry is not the common element; only Dynomap engages spatial layout, and it applies that to tabular features.
